NCP leaders, police scuffle as convoy stopped in Sreemangal
item.description:
Saiful Islam
Police stopped the convoy of National Citizen Party (NCP) leaders in Sreemangal on Wednesday afternoon as they were heading to Habiganj to join a previously announced protest program, triggering a brief scuffle over police barricades.
The confrontation took place around 4:30pm near the Tea Maiden (Cha Kanya) sculpture on the Sreemangal-Shayestaganj road after police blocked the route with trucks and barricades.
NCP Convener Nahid Islam, Chief Organizer (Northern Region) Sarjis Alam, Chief Organizer (Southern Region) and MP Hasnat Abdullah, Chief Coordinator Nasiruddin Patwary and MP Dr Mahmuda Mitu got out of their vehicles and held talks with police officials at the scene.
At one stage, pushing and shoving broke out between police personnel and NCP leaders and activists. Hasnat Abdullah and Nasiruddin Patwary were seen in a scuffle with police as officers attempted to move them away from the barricade.
During an exchange with police, Hasnat questioned the legality of the blockade.
“If you can, provide us with security. If not, we will proceed at our own responsibility. Under what law are you stopping us?” he said.
Police officials cited security concerns, but Hasnat replied: “Who are the security threats? Instead of arresting them, you are blocking our road. You imposed Section 144 in Habiganj and are stopping us in Sreemangal. This is illegal.”
A police officer at the scene told the NCP leaders that “a major incident” could occur if they crossed the barricade.
The NCP convoy later crossed the barricade and resumed its journey to Habiganj.
According to party sources, Nahid, Opposition Chief Whip in parliament; Member Secretary Akhtar Hossain; Sarjis; Hasnat; Nasiruddin; Dr Mahmuda Mitu and other leaders left the Moulvibazar Circuit House for Habiganj around 3pm.
Police later set up barricades using trucks near the Tea Maiden sculpture, halting the convoy and causing traffic congestion, with hundreds of vehicles stranded on both sides of the road.
Moulvibazar Assistant Superintendent of Police (Sreemangal Circle) Md Wahiduzzaman Raju said the leaders had been stopped for security reasons.
The latest incident came a day after NCP leaders alleged that activists of the BNP, Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and Jubo Dal attacked their convoy in Habiganj town following Tuesday’s program, leaving several people injured.
Amid heightened tensions between the BNP and the NCP, the administration-imposed Section 144 in the Habiganj municipal area from Wednesday morning.
Local sources said Chhatra Dal activists allegedly attacked vehicles carrying NCP leaders near Habiganj Town Hall on Tuesday evening. Several vehicles belonging to journalists were also vandalized.
Sarjis Alam and Nasiruddin Patwary reportedly took shelter in a branch of Sonali Bank during the attack before police escorted them to safety.
The NCP later suspended two previously announced “July March” programs in Moulvibazar and instead announced a protest rally in Habiganj, while separate programs by BNP and Chhatra Dal further heightened tensions in the district.

item.title: Trivedi: PM Tarique's India visit key to positive progress
item.description:
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi on Wednesday expressed optimism about the future of bilateral ties, saying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's proposed visit to India would pave the way for progress on outstanding issues, including the renewal of the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty.
Speaking to reporters after separate courtesy meetings with Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Trivedi said discussions covered a range of issues and were held in a positive atmosphere.
"Once Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to India is confirmed and the joint working group sits down with the necessary documents, everything will move in a positive direction," he said.
The envoy said there was no bilateral issue that could not be resolved through dialogue in a way that served the mutual interests of both countries.
"There is no problem that cannot be resolved if it benefits both countries," he said.
On the renewal of the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty, Trivedi said the joint working group of the two countries was already discussing the matter.
"I hope they will meet soon. There is no issue that cannot be resolved. Whatever is necessary in the interests of the people of both countries will be done," he said.
Describing the meetings as constructive, the Indian high commissioner said the discussions focused on issues important to the people of both countries.
"At the end of the day, this is about the people of the two countries. Whatever is necessary for the democracies of both countries, those interests will be taken into consideration," he added.

item.title: Law minister: Govt taken effective initiatives to reduce civil case backlog
item.description:
Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Md Asaduzzaman on Wednesday said the present government has taken effective initiatives to reduce longstanding civil case backlog.
"Various reform initiatives are being implemented to make the judicial process faster, more efficient and more people-friendly. Backlog of cases could be reduced and the efficiency of the judicial process enhanced through the exchange of domestic and international experiences and mutual cooperation," he said.
The minister made the remarks at a seminar titled "Addressing Delays in the Disposal of Civil Cases: Shared Experiences of Bangladesh and Japan" at Judicial Administration Training Institute (JATI). Law and Justice Division and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) jointly organized the seminar, an official release said on Wednesday.
Md Asaduzzaman said that many civil cases in Bangladesh are still pending despite having remained unresolved for many years. The prolonged pendency of these cases has increased the sufferings of litigants and placed an additional burden on the judicial system, he added.
"To address this situation, the government is implementing various reform initiatives, including modernizing the judiciary, expanding Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), introducing technology-driven judicial services, and making the judicial process simpler and more efficient," he further said.
The law minister also said the experiences and cooperation of the Japanese Ministry of Justice and international partners, including the JICA, would play a significant role in strengthening Bangladesh's judicial system.
"Such joint initiatives would create new opportunities for the exchange of knowledge and experiences between the two countries, which would make a positive contribution to enhancing the efficiency of the judicial process," he added.
Speaking as the special guest, Deputy Director-General of the International Cooperation Department of Japan's Ministry of Justice, Kazunori Nose, assured that Japan would continue its cooperation in strengthening and enhancing the capacity of Bangladesh's judicial system.
The keynote papers were presented by Senior Assistant Secretary of the Law and Justice Division Syed Md Shafayet and Professor Wakazono Rei of Japan's Ministry of Justice. Project Director of the relevant project and Additional Secretary of the Law and Justice Division Md Khadem Ul Kayes chaired the seminar.

item.title: Health officials report 534 fresh cases of dengue inflection, 3 deaths overnight
item.description:
Health officials on Wednesday said they recorded 534 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts killing at least three persons in the past 24 hours.
"During the period, (of the 534) 68 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 71 in Chittagong division, 131 in Dhaka division, 56 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 65 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 45 in Khulna division, 37 in Mymensingh division, 30 in Rajshahi division, 26 in Rangpur division and five in Sylhet division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaughts, Bangladesh this year has witnessed so far 50 deaths while the disease inflicted 14,690.
Last year, dengue claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country.
Besides, dengue claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: PM meets Tahsin, who lost sister in Milestone tragedy
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday met Tahsin Abdullah, a schoolboy whose heartwarming smile at the closing ceremony of the Notun Kuri Sports 2025-26 touched millions, a year after the boy lost his elder sister in the Milestone School fighter jet crash.
Learning the heartbreaking story behind the widely shared photograph of the smiling boy on social media, the prime minister met Tahsin and his father Nazmul Haque at the prime minister's office at Bangladesh Secretariat on Wednesday, said PM’s Assistant Press Secretary Gazi Shahriar Pamir.
A photograph of Tahsin during the closing ceremony of the “Notun Kuri Sports 2025-26” at Bangladesh Army Stadium in the capital on July 27 went viral on social media, showing Tahsin in his school uniform stretching out both hands towards the prime minister with an expression of pure joy. But behind that heartwarming smile was a story of deep personal grief.
In July 2025, Tahsin lost his elder sister Tasnia in the tragic fighter jet crash at Milestone School in Uttara. Although both siblings studied at the same school, they were in separate buildings on that fateful day. Tahsin was then a sixth-grade student, while Tasnia was an eighth-grader. The fighter jet crashed into the building where Tasnia was attending classes.
Hearing the deafening explosion, young Tahsin rushed to find his elder sister. After hearing that saline and water were needed, he stood waiting with bottles of saline and water in his small hands for his sister. But that wait never ended.
According to his family, the tragedy changed Tahsin completely. During a healing session after the incident, he wrote: “I am in great pain. I have lost my beloved sister. She died. I miss her so, so much. She was my best friend.”
Since losing his sister, Tahsin's once cheerful and lively smile was rarely seen. But on July 27 was a different day. At the Bangladesh Army Stadium, as Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was moving around the field during the closing ceremony, Tahsin became overwhelmed with joy when the prime minister came near him.
His innocent smile and excitement were captured on camera, and the photograph later spread widely on social media, with many people connecting emotionally with the boy’s happiness.
Later, the prime minister came to know that behind the smiling face in the photograph was a heartbreaking family history. After learning the details, he directed his Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon to take steps to inquire about Tahsin and his family.
As Tahsin arrived at prime minister’s office, the prime minister enquired about Tahsin's studies and ambitions. Tahsin said he wanted to become a successful businessman and do something that would benefit people and attract them.
The prime minister appreciated his dream and advised the young boy to concentrate on his studies, play sports regularly and work with sincerity and dedication to achieve his goals, Pamir said.
During the conversation, Tahsin said football was his favorite sports. The prime minister gifted him a basketball bearing his autograph and a drone set.
After the meeting, an excited Tahsin said he was very happy to meet the prime minister again. He said he never imagined he would get such an opportunity and described the entire experience as a complete surprise. He said he was eagerly waiting to go to school and share the story of meeting the prime minister with his friends.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman also expressed deep sympathy and condolence to Tahsin’s father over the tragic loss of his daughter in the Milestone fighter jet crash.
PM’s Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon, Private Secretary-2 Md Mehedul Islam, Assistant Private Secretary-2 Abdur Rahman Sani, Associate Professor (Orthopedics) Dr Shah Muhammad Aman Ullah, Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony and Amra BNP Poribar Member Secretary Moksedul Momin Mithun were present.

India lower house passes bill raising penalties for exam leaks
item.description:
India’s lower house of parliament approved a bill on Wednesday that would toughen penalties for leaking exam papers, after youth-led protests calling for sweeping reforms forced the education minister to resign.
The legislation would double the maximum jail term for those involved in leaking exam papers to 10 years, and raises the maximum fine to more than $1 million.
Lawmakers approved the bill by a voice vote after a raucous, hours-long debate, according to India’s public broadcaster.
It will next be put to a vote in the upper house, where Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling alliance holds a majority. Modi’s cabinet greenlighted the stricter punishments last week.
The approval follows weeks of mass protests over leaked exam papers and other irregularities, which culminated in the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on Saturday.
The protests, spearheaded by the online Cockroach Janta Party movement, drew massive support from students across the country and presented a major challenge to Modi’s government.
Rahul Gandhi of the main opposition Congress Party said he could relate to the frustration among India’s youth over the country’s education system.
“This was not anger... this was not hatred, this was deep expression of the youth of this country, of the future generation of this country, and I feel that all political parties must respect this expression,” he said in a speech in the house.
Despite rapid economic growth in the world’s most populous country, millions of young people face a shortage of well-paid jobs and fierce competition for careers.
The intense pressure to succeed has fueled a vast network of coaching centers and created opportunities for criminal groups to profit by selling leaked exam questions.
Despite repeated government crackdowns, such leaks have remained a recurring problem in both national and state-level examinations.
Demonstrations against the paper leaks in New Delhi turned violent on July 20 when huge crowds attempted to march towards parliament from the Jantar Mantar protest site.
Police fired tear gas and used batons to disperse the protest, triggering clashes and a wave of detentions.

item.title: France expands mass evacuations as Spain battles wildfires
item.description:
As Spain battled its largest wildfire on record and France carried out one of Europe’s biggest evacuations since World War II, scientists warned that extreme wildfires are becoming more frequent worldwide.
On Tuesday, French authorities evacuated another 4,000 people from Atlantic coast resorts adding to the 220,000 other people fleeing a blazing wildfire in southwest France.
Fresh fires broke out near the Atlantic resort of Grand Crohot west of Bordeaux, prompting authorities to deploy 23 planes and helicopters to contain the flames.
“The situation remains complicated. We’re not out of the woods,” said Sophie Brocas, the top government official in the coastal region of Gironde, where Grand Crohot and Bordeaux are located.
The Gironde wildfire has burned an area four times the size of Paris, and resisted the firefighting efforts of a dozen countries.
In Spain, there was a respite for the evacuees as thousands of residents were allowed to return home after firefighters managed to contain major blazes.
However, authorities remained on alert for a fourth summer heatwave with temperatures expected to exceed 40 degrees Celsius on Wednesday.
The biggest concern for firefighters in Spain was two large fires that had at times come close to merging into a single blaze in wooded hills to the west of Madrid.
In Avila, to the northwest of Madrid, a pyrocumulonimbus cloud was seen over the blaze. Scientists describe these clouds as fire-generated thunderstorms forming over intense heat sources like wildfires or volcanic eruptions.
“We are feeling a lot of anger and helplessness. It’s something inhuman,” 48-year-old gardener David Gonzalez said about the destruction caused by the fires in Avila.
Experts fear that incoming heat waves might cause the blazing fires to worsen.

Russian fencer wins world championship gold under his country flag
item.description:
A Russian has won a gold medal at the World Fencing Championships in Hong Kong, the first since the country was allowed to compete again under its own flag in the combat sport.
Pavel Graudyn, 19, defeated South Korean Do Gyeong-dong 15-7 in the men's individual sabre final on Tuesday, having earlier stunned France's top-seed Sebastien Patrice in the last 16.
It was the first major championship since the International Fencing Federation (FIE) lifted all restrictions on Russian and Belarusian athletes on June 2.
The sanctions had been imposed in 2022 after the invasion of Ukraine and consequent war, with Russian and Belarusian fencers allowed to participate only as neutrals.
The International Olympic Committee (IOC) earlier this month lifted some restrictions allowing Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete in team events and qualifying for the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.
Ukraine slammed the IOC decision as "premature" and "unfounded" after more than four years of conflict since Russia's invasion.
Governing bodies for swimming, gymnastics, judo, taekwondo and wrestling have also recently lifted restrictions on Russian and Belarusian athletes.

Apparel leaders want to source gas from CNG stations amid severe shortage
item.description:
Amid a severe gas shortage triggered by the shutdown of a Floating Storage Regasification Unit (FSRU) terminal in Maheshkhali, the country's two leading apparel trade bodies—the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA)—have urged the government to allow export-oriented garment factories to source Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) in cylinders from filling stations.
In separate letters issued on July 28, the trade associations informed the government that granting factories temporary access to CNG stations until regular gas supplies normalize would help maintain production and export operations.
The appeal follows an order issued on July 27 by Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company, which directed all CNG filling stations to immediately stop selling natural gas in open cylinders or gas cascades to non-authorized vehicles.
Titas stated that such supplies pose severe safety risks and violate the Gas Act 2010 and the Gas Distribution Rules 2026.
Titas warned in its letter that supplying gas in unauthorized cylinders is illegal and highly dangerous, adding that non-compliance could lead to connection disconnections and legal action.
In a letter sent to the President of the Bangladesh CNG Filling Station and Conversion Workshop Owners Association, BGMEA president Mahmud Hasan Khan stated that the readymade garment sector is the primary engine of the national economy, driving maximum export earnings, generating millions of jobs, and earning foreign exchange.
He noted that the shutdown of one of the two FSRU LNG terminals in Maheshkhali has caused a severe gas crisis across industrial hubs. Gas pressure in many factories has dropped to zero PSI, making it increasingly difficult to sustain production and deliver shipments to international buyers on schedule.
The BGMEA requested that factories with urgent operational needs be granted temporary permission to collect gas in cylinders from CNG filling stations to safeguard production and honor export commitments.
The association added that Titas's recent order has made many filling stations reluctant to supply gas in cylinders.
BKMEA seeks ministry intervention
Meanwhile, in a notice to its members, the BKMEA stated that following Titas's directive, the association's president discussed the matter with the Secretary of the Energy and Mineral Resources Division.
According to BKMEA, after explaining that disruptions to gas supply in export-oriented industries would severely harm production and exports, the Energy Secretary instructed Titas's managing director to take necessary measures so that export-oriented factories can continue sourcing gas from CNG filling stations as before.
The trade body advised member factories to strictly adhere to government regulations and safety guidelines while collecting gas, and urged those with alternative LMG (mobile gas) setups to utilize them at full capacity.
The BKMEA noted that the current gas shortage may persist until August 8, after which conditions are expected to gradually normalize. It added that it remains in regular contact with relevant authorities to monitor the situation.

item.title: BUFT inaugurates 'Abdullah Hil Rakib Auditorium'
item.description:
BGMEA University of Fashion & Technology (BUFT) inaugurated the Abdullah Hil Rakib Auditorium at its campus on July 29, honoring the late industry leader, education advocate, and former member of the university's board of trustees for his enduring contributions to higher education and Bangladesh's apparel sector.
The inauguration ceremony was attended by Faruque Hassan, chairman of the board of trustees of BUFT and former president of BGMEA; Md Moshiul Azam Shajal, member of BoT; Mohammed Nasir, member of BoT; Mohammad Sohel Sadat, chairman, Shin-Shin Group; Dr Afroza Shahin, managing director of TEAM Group; Abdullah Hil Nakib, deputy managing director of TEAM Group; Sharmeen Hassan, director of Giant Group; Prof Engr Ayub Nabi Khan, vice chancellor (designate) of BUFT; acting pro vice chancellor and treasurer; the registrar; as well as faculty members, officials, students, and distinguished guests.
The program began with the unveiling of the newly named auditorium, followed by a documentary highlighting the life, leadership, and lasting contributions of Abdullah Hil Rakib to Bangladesh's readymade garment industry and his unwavering commitment to education and institutional development.
The event concluded with a Doa seeking eternal peace for the departed soul and blessings for the continued progress of the university.

item.title: Standard Chartered, BMMOA to deliver exclusive banking privileges for Bangladesh’s mariners
item.description:
Standard Chartered Bangladesh has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Bangladesh Merchant Marine Officers’ Association (BMMOA) to introduce an exclusive suite of banking privileges for Bangladeshi mariners, reaffirming the bank’s commitment to delivering customer-centric solutions for Bangladesh’s diverse professional communities.
Mariners spend extended periods away from home while continuing to manage their families’ financial needs, support loved ones and plan for their long-term financial future.
The nature of their profession demands banking solutions that are accessible, flexible and tailored to a globally mobile lifestyle.
Responding to these unique needs, Standard Chartered has developed a dedicated banking proposition that brings together Priority Banking privileges, preferential lending rates, processing fee waivers on retail lending facilities, annual fee waivers on eligible credit & debit card, and a range of exclusive banking benefits.
Eligible new and existing mariner clients will also enjoy dedicated onboarding benefits, with newly onboarded clients eligible for cashback upon meeting the applicable eligibility and balance requirements.
Together, these benefits are designed to make banking simpler, more convenient and more rewarding for mariners at every stage of their financial journey.
Lutful Habib, managing director & head of wealth and retail banking, Standard Chartered Bangladesh, said: “At Standard Chartered Wealth & Retail Banking, we believe meaningful banking begins with understanding the people we serve. Mariners spend long periods away from home yet remain intricately connected to the financial wellbeing of their families and the country. Through this partnership, we are bringing them a dedicated set of banking privileges designed around their unique professional journey and financial needs.”
Capt Md Anam Chowdhury, president, Bangladesh Merchant Marine Officers’ Association, said: “Standard Chartered has recognized the distinct needs of mariners and developed this collaboration around the realities of their profession. Mariners spend long periods away from home while continuing to support their families and contribute to the country. Through this partnership, our members will receive relevant banking privileges that can make their financial lives simpler, more convenient and more rewarding.”
The MoU signing ceremony was attended by senior representatives from both organizations.
Representing Standard Chartered Bangladesh were Faisal Haque, head of priority and wealth management; Rana Shahid Hassan, head of deposits and digital banking; Rahanuma Tasrian Omee, senior product manager, deposits; Azizur Rahman, branch manager, Chittagong main branch; and Sajib Kazi, branch manager, Nasirabad Branch.
Representing the Bangladesh Merchant Marine Officers’ Association were Capt Md Anam Chowdhury, president; Mar. Engr. Md Shakwat Hossain, general secretary; and Capt Mohammed Habibur Rahman, senior member.
The partnership with BMMOA reflects the bank’s commitment to combining global expertise with local insight to deliver relevant financial solutions that create lasting value for its clients.

item.title: Banglalink's AI-powered digital lifestyle brand RYZE wins global award for AI Innovation
item.description:
Banglalink's AI-powered digital lifestyle brand RYZE has received the AI Innovation Award at the Global Conference on AI Leadership and Flagship Prestige Awards 2026, in recognition for its contribution to advancing artificial intelligence solutions that empower young people, enhance employability, and prepare the workforce of the future.
The Global Conference on AI Leadership and Flagship Prestige Awards 2026, held at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Dhaka recently, was jointly organized by the International AI Innovation and Leadership Consortium (IAILC) and the Universal Humanity Foundation (UHF), Canada.
The conference brought together technology experts, policymakers, researchers, academics and industry leaders from home and abroad to discuss artificial intelligence, digital leadership and related emerging technologies.
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon attended the event as chief guest and highlighted the importance of effectively utilizing AI to improve performance and efficiency, emphasizing that embracing artificial intelligence is the demand of the modern era.
"This international recognition reflects Banglalink's commitment to leveraging artificial intelligence to create meaningful value for our customers and communities," said Taimur Rahman, chief corporate and regulatory affairs officer of Banglalink.
"Through RYZE, we are making artificial intelligence more accessible by enabling young people to build future-ready skills. As the country's leading digital operator, we are committed to driving digital innovation that promotes inclusion, enhances employability, and contributes to Bangladesh's digital transformation."
As Banglalink's AI-powered digital lifestyle brand, RYZE was recognized for developing an AI ecosystem that makes artificial intelligence practical and accessible for students and young professionals.
Through Vocalyze, users receive real-time AI-powered spoken English coaching with instant feedback on pronunciation, fluency, and confidence, while CV-Ryzer helps them create professional, ATS-friendly resumes that improve their employability.
Alongside these platforms, RYZE continues to introduce AI-powered tools that promote digital literacy, productivity, creativity, and responsible AI adoption, helping young people build future-ready competencies.

item.title: NRB Bank appoints Anwar Uddin and Kimiwa Saddat as AMDs
item.description:
NRB Bank PLC has recently appointed Anwar Uddin and Kimiwa Saddat as additional managing directors (AMDs) to strengthen its executive leadership team and drive sustainable growth.
Anwar Uddin, who previously served as deputy managing director at the bank, has been promoted to additional managing director in recognition of his leadership and contributions.
With a banking career spanning nearly four decades, Uddin started as probationary officer at NCC Bank Ltd in 1987.
He later joined Southeast Bank Limited in 1996, rising to deputy managing director while managing corporate banking, credit administration, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
Meanwhile, Kimiwa Saddat has joined NRB Bank PLC as additional managing director and chief business officer (AMD & CBO), effective July 29.
Bringing over 23 years of diversified banking experience, Saddat previously served as managing director & CEO (current charge) at Community Bank Bangladesh PLC.
His career also includes key senior positions at Meghna Bank PLC, HSBC Bangladesh, The City Bank PLC, Eastern Bank PLC, and GSP Finance Company (Bangladesh) Ltd.
Saddat holds both a BBA and an MBA in Finance from the University of Dhaka and is a Certified Financial Consultant (CFC), Canada.
In addition to his corporate role, he serves as an Adjunct Faculty Member in the Department of Finance at the University of Dhaka.

item.title: HSBC celebrates Saudia's journey in Bangladesh
item.description:
The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (HSBC) Bangladesh has recently hosted an exclusive event ‘Powering global connectivity’ - an evening celebrating Saudia’s 46 years journey in Bangladesh and the enduring partnership between Saudia and HSBC at a hotel in the capital.
The event was graced by Afroza Khanam, MP, Minister for Civil Aviation and Tourism, as chief guest, Abdullah Ibn Dhafer Ibn Ubayya, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Bangladesh as special guest, Tanvir Ghani, special assistant to the prime minister, investment and capital market affairs, Prime Minister's Office as special guest, Mohammed Alsilimani, AVP treasury & taxation, Saudia as guest of honour, Salman A Alali, Saudia country manager in Bangladesh, and Md Mahbub ur Rahman, chief executive officer, HSBC Bangladesh.
Saudia, the national flag carrier of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, has a remarkable legacy in serving the vibrant Bangladeshi diaspora in the Kingdom through its extensive flight network, connecting families, facilitating cross-border possibilities and enabling thousands of Bangladeshis for pilgrimage.
For over four decades, Saudia has played a vital role in linking Bangladesh with the kingdom of Saudi Arabia, serving millions of passengers, including pilgrims, expatriate workers, business travelers, and tourists.
Saudia is the largest foreign carrier in Bangladesh, operating 32 weekly flights.
The event recognized six organizations and stakeholders who have contributed to strengthening air connectivity, facilitating international trade, supporting Hajj and Umrah travel, and enhancing financial collaboration between Bangladesh and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Jamaat asks EC to lift MPO teacher election bar
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on Wednesday demanded that the Election Commission withdraw its proposed provision barring MPO-listed teachers from contesting local government elections and cancel the contractual appointment of an additional secretary over “political affiliation”.
A six-member Jamaat delegation, led by its Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar, sat in a meeting with Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin at the Nirbachan Bhaban in Dhaka's Agargaon and submitted a letter to the CEC.
Election Commissioners Abdur Rahmanel Masud and Tahmida Ahmad, along with EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed, were also present at the meeting in the morning.
According to a letter submitted to the CEC, Jamaat also demanded consideration of its previous opinions regarding the local government election code of conduct, which were placed before the Election Commission on June 30 last.
In the letter, Jamaat said the EC has sent a proposal to the Ministry of Local Government declaring MPO-affiliated teachers ineligible to contest in local government elections.
If the proposed provision is implemented, several lakhs of teachers and employees of more than 30,000 MPO-affiliated educational institutions in the country will be deprived of the opportunity to participate in local government elections, which is inconsistent with the principles of equality and non-discrimination enshrined in Articles 27 and 28 of the Constitution, it added.
“So, we believe that the proposed provision needs to be reconsidered and withdrawn or amended so that the constitutional right of eligible citizens to political participation remains intact,” it said.
Jamaat also demanded the immediate cancellation of the recent contractual appointment of 67-year-old Md Shamsul Alam as an additional secretary to the EC Secretariat, alleging that he had links with a political party.
The party claimed that media reports regarding his alleged political affiliation have raised questions among people about the neutrality of the Election Commission.
The Jamaat delegation also included Assistant Secretaries General Dr AHM Hamidur Rahman Azad, Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair and Moazzem Hossain Helal, members of its central working committee Jasim Uddin Sarkar and Shishir Mohammad Monir.

Accused on life support in ICU, handcuffs spark fresh controversy
item.description:
Mizanur Rahman has remained in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of the Department of Critical Care Medicine at Dhaka Medical College Hospital since 14 June. Physicians placed him on life support two days after his admission.

Speaking to Prothom Alo while sitting outside the ICU on Saturday, 25 July, Mizanur Rahman's mother, Matoara Begum, said, “For the first two days after he was admitted to hospital, he kept crying out calling “mother”.

Since then, he has had no awareness of the world around him. He does not even recognise me anymore. His entire body is paralysed.”

A photograph of Mizanur Rahman recently circulated on Facebook. The image shows a thick tube attached to his throat and another tube inserted into his nose.

As he lies in bed, his right hand is secured with handcuffs attached to a thick rope, while an oximeter remains clipped to one of the fingers on that hand.

Mizanur Rahman's wife, Salma Jahan, confirmed to Prothom Alo that the photograph circulating on Facebook is indeed of her husband.

However, neither she nor any other family member knows who took the photograph inside the ICU or how it was leaked.

Salma Jahan said, “On Monday, when the physicians informed us that my husband's condition had become extremely critical, we requested that the police remove the handcuffs, and they agreed. Before that, we had repeatedly asked them to remove the handcuffs, but the officers on duty always said that the rules did not allow it.”

Mizanur Rahman remained handcuffed throughout an entire month in the ICU.

Mizanur Rahman, 48, is the former vice-chairman of Patuakhali sadar upazila parishad and was a member of the Patuakhali District Committee of the Awami League, whose activities have been banned now.

Following the fall of the Awami League government on 5 August 2024 during the mass uprising, his house in Patuakhali came under attack.

Mizanur Rahman faces multiple criminal cases, including charges of murder and attempted murder.

After his arrest 11 months ago in connection with a case filed at Paltan police station in Dhaka, the authorities detained him at Kashimpur Prison in Gazipur.

According to Salma Jahan, Mizanur Rahman fell ill at Kashimpur Prison on 9 June. However, the prison authorities did not inform the family. They learnt of his condition through the relative of another inmate who was acquainted with him.

The authorities initially admitted Mizanur Rahman to Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital in Gazipur.

They later transferred him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital, and then back to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where physicians subsequently admitted him to the ICU.

Mizanur Rahman is the former vice-chairman of Patuakhali sadar upazila parishad and was a member of the Patuakhali District Committee of the Awami League, whose activities have now been banned.

Salma Jahan said, “My husband secures bail in one case, only to be shown arrested in another. They are persecuting him for political reasons. At this point, we do not even know whether he will survive. Our family has also become physically and mentally exhausted.”

Mizanur Rahman is the only brother among five sisters. Since their father died 20 years ago, the entire family has depended on him. Outside the ICU at Dhaka Medical College Hospital, his mother, wife, sisters and other relatives take turns staying on mats spread across the floor.

The authorities arrested Mizanur Rahman in Dhaka on 14 September last year in connection with a murder case. The First Information Report (FIR) identified him as a “suspected accused” in that case.

His wife, Salma Jahan, also spent six months in Patuakhali district prison and Kashimpur women's prison in connection with three separate cases. She is now out on bail.

Mizanur Rahman's mother, Matoara BegumHe has had no awareness of the world around him. He does not even recognise me anymore. His entire body is paralysed

She previously served as chairman of Kalikapur Union Parishad in Patuakhali sadar upazila and as organising secretary of the district unit of the Krishak League.

Meanwhile, while Mizanur Rahman remained in Kashimpur Central Prison, the authorities showed him arrested in several additional cases.

His lawyer in Dhaka, HM Sarwar Hossain, told Prothom Alo that Mizanur Rahman has so far secured bail in a total of eight cases filed in Patuakhali and Dhaka.

While he was critically ill and receiving treatment in the ICU, the authorities summoned him to court on 23 June as a suspected accused in another case. The court has now scheduled a virtual hearing for 30 July.

“This patient is in no condition to escape”          

Prothom Alo spoke to several physicians working in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of the Department of Critical Care Medicine. Speaking on condition of anonymity, the physicians said the patient remains on life support and that there is no way to say with certainty whether he will survive.

His condition has deteriorated critically on several occasions, prompting the medical team to advise the family to prepare themselves mentally for the worst.

Several police officers have been deployed outside the ICU in three shifts. Although the physicians requested that the handcuffs be removed, the officers repeatedly refused, saying that "the rules do not permit it".

When Prothom Alo asked several police officers on duty outside the ICU on Saturday afternoon about keeping the patient handcuffed, they said only that they were carrying out orders from their superiors. They added that they had no authority to remove the handcuffs on their own initiative.

Inspector General of Prisons Brigadier General Syed Md Motaher Hossain told Prothom Alo that handcuffs are primarily used to prevent an accused person from escaping and to ensure security.

He said that, in the case of accused persons receiving treatment in hospital, the handcuffs are removed if the attending physicians raise an objection.

One of the physicians responsible for the ICU told Prothom Alo, “The handcuffs interfered with treatment in the ICU, including procedures such as inserting a cannula. The rope attached to the handcuffs was not properly sterilised either. Most importantly, this patient has never been in a condition where he could possibly escape. Keeping a patient handcuffed in the ICU is extremely inhumane.”

Asked whether Mizanur Rahman could have escaped from the ICU, Inspector General Syed Md Motaher Hossain said, “We do not expect a seriously ill person to remain in handcuffs either. However, we still have certain shortcomings. Prisoners receive treatment in different hospitals and different wards. The issue of security always remains. Officers assigned to guard accused persons in hospital often find themselves in difficult situations.”

Recurring controversy over the use of handcuffs

A similar controversy recently arose after former Industries Minister and leader of Awami League, whose activities are now banned, Nurul Majid Mahmud Humayun was kept in handcuffs while receiving treatment in hospital.

He died on 29 September last year at the age of 75 while undergoing treatment in the ICU of Dhaka Medical College Hospital. At the time, photographs showing him lying in a hospital bed while handcuffed circulated widely on social media.

On 3 July 2018, the High Court ruled that the authorities must not misuse the law governing the use of handcuffs on arrested persons. The Court also instructed the relevant authorities to exercise caution when deciding whether to use handcuffs.

Speaking to the media at the time, Abu Obaidur Rahman, the lawyer who argued the case on behalf of the Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST), said that the police should follow the provisions of the Police Regulations of Bengal (PRB) when deciding whether to use handcuffs. He added that placing handcuffs on anyone outside the scope of those regulations would constitute a violation of human rights.

Regulation 330 of the Police Regulations of Bengal sets out the rules governing the use of handcuffs.

It prohibits imposing any greater restraint than is necessary solely to prevent an accused person from escaping. The regulation permits the use of handcuffs only in specific circumstances—for example, if the prisoner is physically strong and accused of a violent offence, is a known habitual offender, is likely to create trouble, if the journey is particularly long, or if a large number of prisoners are being escorted.

In 2017, the authorities kept a student of Jahangirnagar University handcuffed while he was receiving treatment in hospital after his arrest. After the High Court took judicial notice of a report published in the “The Daily Star”, it issued a rule on 29 May 2017.

According to Salma Jahan, Mizanur Rahman fell ill at Kashimpur Prison on 9 June. However, the prison authorities did not inform the family. They learnt of his condition through the relative of another inmate who was acquainted with him.

The Court also summoned the Officer-in-Charge of Ashulia police station to explain why the student had remained handcuffed during medical treatment. Through the rule, the Court sought an explanation as to why keeping a patient handcuffed while undergoing treatment should not be declared unlawful.

On 22 January 2023, 10 Supreme Court lawyers served legal notices on three secretaries to the government, the Inspector General of Police and the Inspector General of Prisons, urging them to take the necessary steps to stop the unlawful practice of using shackles and handcuffs on prisoners and arrested persons and to formulate a specific policy on the matter. Asad Uddin, a lawyer at the Supreme Court, served the notice on behalf of the 10 lawyers.

Asad Uddin told Prothom Alo that the legal notice requested the government to stop the unlawful use of handcuffs and shackles on accused persons and to formulate a guideline or policy on the issue within 15 working days.

He added that the High Court later heard a writ petition filed by senior lawyer Kayser Kamal and issued a rule concerning the formation of a committee to prepare guidelines on the use of handcuffs on prisoners and detainees.

Through the rule, the Court asked why it should not direct the authorities to establish such a committee.

On 30 January 2023, the High Court issued another rule asking why the use of the relevant provisions of the Prisons Act, 1894, and the Jail Code in an “arbitrary and unreasonable” manner to place ordinary prisoners in shackles and handcuffs should not be declared unlawful.

The High Court Bench issued the rule after holding a preliminary hearing on a writ petition challenging the legality of using those provisions to impose shackles and handcuffs “arbitrarily and unreasonably”.

Lawyer Kayser Kamal, who now serves as the Deputy Speaker of the National Parliament, filed that writ petition.

On 3 December 2023, Nahid Sultana, the wife of Md Aminur Rahman, filed a writ petition challenging the legality of providing medical treatment to her husband while he remained in shackles.

Aminur Rahman was a leader of Jubo Dal in Jashore. Kayser Kamal represented the petitioner. At the time, photographs of Aminur lying in a hospital bed with shackles on his legs also spread widely on Facebook.

Inspector General of Prisons Brigadier General Syed Md Motaher Hossain told Prothom Alo that the authorities have not yet formulated any guideline or policy governing the use of handcuffs.

Physicians also believe that the authorities urgently need to introduce a specific policy governing the use of handcuffs on patients receiving medical treatment, particularly those in intensive care units (ICUs).

EUROPE-WEATHER/WILDFIRE-SPAIN

A major blaze in central Spain has stabilised, Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said on Wednesday, in a rare reprieve as soaring temperatures in France and Spain increased the threat from wildfires in both countries.

Blazes have forced large-scale evacuations of people, scorched through forests and killed wildlife in Spain and France over the past days, and the minister had warned of "three tough days" ahead, with strong winds and high temperatures.

But Grande-Marlaska later said authorities had now lifted all evacuation and shelter-in-place orders in Avila province, though some curbs remained in parts of the Madrid area.

Authorities meanwhile warned of another fire in the northwestern Spanish province of Zamora. They issued an evacuation order for six towns and asked about 1,000 people to shelter in place.

Spain's weather agency AEMET said temperatures were expected to reach 40 degrees Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit) on Wednesday in at least six regions, which have been placed on orange alert, the second-highest level.

Firefighters wary of new temperature rise

In France, temperatures in the southwest, hit by devastating fires, were expected to rise from around 33 C on Tuesday to peak at 42 C, according to Meteo France, while dry winds in the afternoon could stoke flames.

French firefighters kept a major blaze west of Bordeaux stable overnight. And near Bordeaux's airport, which has remained open, tramway services resumed and hotels reopened.

But officials warned the wildfires were far from over. The municipality of Lege-Cap-Ferret flagged several flare-ups in the area, adding that firefighters had managed to stabilise them. BFM journalists also reported more flare-ups in the region.

"We remain vigilant of course today, considering the forecast weather conditions, with a new rise in temperatures and higher wind speeds in the afternoon," firefighter commander Matthieu Jomain told reporters earlier in the day.

Meanwhile, the EU's emergency response centre warned that Greece, Italy and Central Europe were also set to face a heightened wildfire risk in the coming weeks.

Evacuations and shock at ruined homes

The impact on the forests has been widespread. The wildfire in the Landes area west of Bordeaux, a popular tourist destination, has devastated 42,000 hectares (104,000 acres) of mainly pine trees.

Authorities have evacuated about 220,000 people, including holidaymakers and local residents, as the fire threatened the Cap Ferret peninsula on the Atlantic coast, only accessible by one road.

Raphael Fohanno could not believe what had happened to his parents' house in the small beach town of Biscarrosse, also hit by wildfires in southwestern France.

"It’s a shock, thinking that just an hour earlier I’d been in my room and everything and now, there’s nothing left,” 18-year-old Fohanno said. His parents and sister had been evacuated by helicopter while he was out of the house.

Fire in Spain's Castellon rages for fifth day

From Thursday onwards, danger levels in southwestern France appear likely to decrease thanks to some thunderstorms, lower temperatures and increased humidity, but will remain high in the southeast, Meteo France said.

Four people were arrested in recent days in the area, one on suspicion of stealing jewellery from evacuated houses, two for allegedly stealing food from an evacuation centre in Bordeaux, and one for pretending to be a therapist and offering paid sessions to evacuees, police said.

While the situation had improved in the central provinces of Avila and Madrid, a blaze in eastern Castellon remained out of control after burning more than 10,000 hectares as weather conditions triggered several flare-ups.

Around 10,000 evacuated residents were still unable to return to their homes in Castellon. The fire's perimeter is currently estimated at 75.5 km (47 miles), regional authorities said as the fire entered its fifth day on Wednesday.

Deer killed in spanish forest

Europe, the world's fastest-warming continent, has endured record-breaking heatwaves this year, as human-driven climate change is intensifying the heat and drought that allow wildfires to spread faster.

More frequent and intense heatwaves are causing thousands of excess deaths and increasingly disrupting everyday life, from snarling road and rail travel to hindering river shipping.

Highlighting the devastation on the countryside and wildlife, Reuters drone footage from El Tiemblo, in Spain's Avila province, near Madrid, showed charred deer carcasses in a forest burnt to ashes.

A Madrid resident who gave her name as Cintia was horrified by the scene in El Tiemblo, a place she has often visited.

"We love this, the wildlife, everything around us. We used to bring food up for the animals because they’re from here. They belong to this land," she said. "And look where it is today.”

item.title: Jamaat asks EC to allow MPO teachers in local elections, seeks removal of additional secretary
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on Wednesday called on the Election Commission to withdraw its proposed provision barring MPO-listed teachers from contesting local government elections and to revoke the contractual appointment of an additional secretary over alleged political affiliation.

A six-member Jamaat delegation, led by its Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar, sat in a meeting with Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin at the Nirbachan Bhaban in the city's Agargaon and submitted a letter to the CEC.

Election Commissioners Abdur Rahmanel Masud and Tahmida Ahmad, along with EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed, were also present at the meeting in the morning.

According to a letter submitted to the CEC, Jamaat also demanded consideration of its previous opinions regarding the local government election code of conduct which were placed before the Election Commission on 30 June last.

In the letter, Jamaat said the EC has sent a proposal to the Ministry of Local Government declaring MPO-affiliated teachers ineligible to contest in local government elections.

If the proposed provision is implemented, several lakhs of teachers and employees of more than 30,000 MPO-affiliated educational institutions in the country will be deprived of the opportunity to participate in local government elections, which is inconsistent with the principles of equality and non-discrimination enshrined in Articles 27 and 28 of the Constitution, it added.

“So, we believe that the proposed provision needs to be reconsidered and withdrawn or amended so that the constitutional right of eligible citizens to political participation remains intact,” it said.

Jamaat also demanded the immediate cancellation of the recent contractual appointment of 67-year-old Md Shamsul Alam as an additional secretary to the EC Secretariat, alleging that he had links with a political party.

The party claimed that media reports regarding his alleged political affiliation have raised questions among people about the neutrality of the Election Commission.

Briefing reporters after the meeting, Mia Golam Parwar said the delegation discussed four demands with the Commission. "We met the Election Commission to discuss our demands aimed at ensuring the upcoming local government elections are fair, neutral, transparent and credible," he said.

Raising the fourth demand, he said they asked the EC to make the administrators appointed to local government bodies on political considerations ineligible to contest local government elections.

Regarding Shamsul Alam's appointment, Parwar alleged that appointing a politically affiliated person to a constitutional body like the Election Commission would undermine its neutrality as he had served as a member of the BNP''s electoral constituency delimitation committee.

The Jamaat leader alleged that the appointment was intended to influence the upcoming local government elections in favour of the ruling party.

The EC told the delegation that it had not been aware of Shamsul Alam's alleged political affiliation and that the contractual appointment had been made by the government. “But the EC could have objected to the appointment,” he said.

Parwar criticised ministers for making differing statements about the possible timing of local government elections.

He also criticised the EC over the publication of the gazette notification declaring BNP leader Sarwar Alamgir elected from Chattogram-2 on the same day the Supreme Court delivered its verdict.

Parwar alleged that the Commission had acted under political pressure by issuing the gazette without waiting for the signed copy of the court order.

“Their body language reflected that they did it under pressure,” he added.

Responding to a question, Parwar said they did not discuss the parliamentary membership of its expelled Satkhira-4 lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam in the meeting.

"We have already written to both the Speaker and the Election Commission. Expulsion from the party is the highest disciplinary action we can take. The issue of parliamentary membership is constitutional and falls under the jurisdiction of the Speaker and the Election Commission," he said.

The Jamaat delegation also included Assistant Secretaries General Dr AHM Hamidur Rahman Azad, Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair and Moazzem Hossain Helal, members of its central working committee Jasim Uddin Sarkar and Shishir Mohammad Monir.

Having made his senior debut in 2010 as an 18-year-old, Neymar quickly became the face of a new generation of Brazilian football. He represented his country at 2014, 2018, 2022 and 2026 FIFA World Cups, though the coveted world title always eluded him.

His international journey included unforgettable highs and heartbreaking setbacks—from missing the end of the 2014 World Cup through injury after Brazil reached the semifinals, to the dramatic penalty-shootout exits in 2022 and the stunning last-16 elimination in 2026.

Although he never lifted the World Cup or the Copa America, Neymar's trophy cabinet with Brazil includes the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, where he inspired the hosts to victory and was named the tournament's best player, and the Olympic gold medal at the Rio 2016 Games, when he scored the decisive penalty in the final against Germany.

item.title: HIV prevention medicines offer hope as access remains biggest hurdle
item.description:
Long-acting HIV prevention medicines could dramatically reduce new HIV infections worldwide, but ensuring affordable and equitable access remains the biggest challenge, global health leaders, researchers, pharmaceutical executives and community advocates said on Tuesday at the 26th International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2026).
For countries such as Bangladesh, where the overall HIV burden remains relatively low but prevention among key populations remains crucial, the key question is whether these new medicines can be made affordable and integrated into existing health systems.
The issue took center stage during a high-level roundtable that brought together International AIDS Society (IAS) President Dr Beatriz Grinsztejn, representatives from ViiV Healthcare, Gilead Sciences, MSD, Unitaid, community organizations and implementation scientists to discuss how scientific breakthroughs can be translated into real-world public health impact.
Opening the discussion, Dr Grinsztejn described the current moment as "a remarkable era" for HIV prevention, citing encouraging results from the PURPOSE 1 and PURPOSE 2 trials of long-acting pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP).
But she stressed that scientific progress alone is not enough.
"Scientific innovation only matters if people can access it," she said, echoing the Brazilian Ministry of Health's message that "innovation without access is not innovation, it is injustice."
Jean van Wyk, chief medical officer of ViiV Healthcare, said injectable cabotegravir is becoming an increasingly important HIV prevention option and reaffirmed the company's commitment to expanding access.
He noted that ViiV signed a licensing agreement with the Medicines Patent Pool within three months of regulatory approval, allowing three generic manufacturers to begin developing affordable versions expected to reach markets by 2028.
Until then, the company has committed to supplying at least two million doses of long-acting PrEP at a non-profit price for lower-middle-income countries beginning in 2025.
Brazil has also recommended incorporating injectable cabotegravir into its public health system.
Presenting findings from pilot implementation projects in South Africa, Elzette Rousseau of the Desmond Tutu Health Foundation said demand for injectable HIV prevention has exceeded expectations.
Across the projects, nearly three-quarters of participants chose injectable PrEP over daily oral pills, while long-acting lenacapavir showed particularly high acceptability.
Jared Baeten, senior vice president at Gilead Sciences, described the approval of twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir as one of the most significant advances in HIV prevention in decades.
He said the PURPOSE 1 trial reported no HIV infections among women receiving lenacapavir, while PURPOSE 2 also demonstrated very high efficacy among men and gender-diverse populations.
Baeten added that Gilead pursued simultaneous regulatory submissions around the world, enabling countries such as Zambia and Eswatini to receive the medicine almost at the same time as wealthier nations — a first for an antiretroviral drug.
To bridge the gap before generic production begins, Gilead has committed enough lenacapavir to protect three million people and expects around 600,000 individuals to be receiving it for HIV prevention by the end of this year.
Despite the scientific breakthroughs, community leaders warned that implementation—not efficacy—will determine success.
Adaobi Lisa Olisa of the Nigerian advocacy organization Root to Rise said communities must be placed at the center of HIV prevention programs.
Olisa said the challenge was implementation rather than science.
"The science is not failing," she said, adding that trust, awareness and community leadership are essential for people to embrace new prevention technologies.
She argued that governments and donors must invest not only in medicines but also in delivery systems, education and demand generation to ensure equitable uptake.
MSD researcher Eliav Barr presented new data on islatravir, an investigational once-monthly oral PrEP pill currently under development.
Phase II trials suggest the medicine begins providing protection within an hour after administration and could be distributed through community health workers without requiring specialized clinical infrastructure.
The session concluded with a debate over access in middle-income countries, particularly those that hosted clinical trials but remain excluded from voluntary licensing agreements.
Representatives from Health GAP questioned the ethics of recruiting participants for research in countries such as Brazil while limiting access through tiered pricing instead of allowing generic production.
Industry representatives defended bridge supply programs, differential pricing and local manufacturing partnerships while regulatory approvals continue.
The discussion underscored a growing consensus that long-acting HIV prevention medicines could transform the global response to HIV, but only if countries can make them affordable and accessible to those who need them most.

Who is David Imon, Chittagong's alleged underworld figure?
item.description:
After months of investigation, law enforcement agencies on Wednesday arrested alleged Chittagong crime figure Mobarak Hossain Imon, widely known as David Imon, in Jessore following what police described as an intelligence-led operation.
Jessore Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime) Mirajul Islam confirmed the arrest to Dhaka Tribune on Wednesday afternoon.
Police allege that Imon was a key figure in an extortion network targeting businesses across Chittagong, demanding a one-time payment of Tk2 crore along with Tk10 lakh every month. Authorities say his arrest followed months of coordinated efforts by intelligence and law enforcement agencies across the country.
Earlier this month, a video allegedly linked to Imon's extortion demands went viral on social media. Several audio and video recordings containing alleged death threats and extortion demands also circulated widely online, triggering public concern and intensifying pressure on law enforcement agencies to arrest him.
A team from the Chittagong District Police arrested Imon along with five associates, all of whom police allege are armed shooters. Investigators say Imon has gained notoriety over the past two years in connection with multiple extortion, intimidation and violent crime cases.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune on Wednesday evening, Chittagong District Police Superintendent Masud Alam said Imon is an accused in at least 15 criminal cases and is believed to be a close associate of fugitive crime figure Sajjad Ali, also known as Boro Sajjad, who police say is currently living abroad.
"Imon is being questioned, and we expect to recover important evidence. He is accused in several cases involving extortion, murder and other serious crimes. Legal proceedings will proceed in accordance with the law," Masud Alam said.
He added that police would brief the media on the case at a press conference scheduled for Thursday morning.
According to police, Boro Sajjad's criminal network consists of around 50 armed associates and shooters. Investigators allege that Imon and another associate, Mohammad Raihan, regularly collected extortion on Sajjad's behalf while Sajjad directed operations from abroad.
Mobarak Hossain Imon is the son of Md Musa of Kanchannagar in Fatikchhari upazila of Chittagong.
According to police records, he is an accused in at least 15 criminal cases, including the March 30, 2025 Bakalia double murder case and the May 23, 2025 murder of alleged criminal Dhakaiya Akbar near Patenga Sea Beach.
Police claim Imon had access to between 15 and 20 firearms and was skilled in using weapons. Investigators also allege that he arranged armed criminals and motorcycles used in the Bakalia double murder.
Senior police officials say that after Sajjad Hossain, also known as Chhoto Sajjad, was imprisoned, leadership of the criminal network in Chittagong shifted to Imon and Mohammad Raihan.
Investigators say an audio recording that went viral on social media on January 26 captured Imon allegedly threatening a man named Aziz Uddin.
"Even if you have 50,000 police guarding you, I'll come to your house and kill you. Just as I shot your brother in front of 10,000 people."
On May 10, Imon allegedly threatened journalist Biplob Dey Partha, demanding Tk50 lakh and warning that he would be shot within 24 hours if the money was not paid. The journalist later filed a General Diary (GD) with Kotwali Police Station.
Police also allege that on July 13, Imon led an attack on the office of internet service provider Digital Dot Net (DDN) on the Chandanpura-Bakalia Access Road in Chittagong. Investigators say that after failing to secure an extortion payment of Tk2 crore, the attackers vandalized the office and looted Tk35 lakh. Video footage of the attack later spread widely on social media.
According to investigators, two days before the attack Imon called businessman Adil Bin Mamun from a foreign phone number and allegedly said:
"If you want to do business, you must pay Tk2 crore upfront and Tk10 lakh every month. From now on, we will control the business."
Imon's arrest has been welcomed by many residents and business owners in Chittagong, several of whom said they hoped it would help curb extortion and organized crime in the city.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune, Chittagong resident Shamsuddin Ilias said the viral videos had created widespread panic among residents. He said many other dangerous criminals remain active and urged authorities to bring not only the criminals but also their patrons to justice in order to dismantle organized criminal networks.
"I had heard many times that he would be arrested. Finally, it has happened, and that itself is a relief," he said.
Businessman Adil Bin Mamun, who claims to be one of the victims of the alleged extortion, said business owners had been living in constant fear because of Imon's activities.
"We have been living in fear because of these threats. I hope this arrest allows us to run our businesses safely again and sends a strong message to others involved in extortion," he said.

item.title: Tree fair gains momentum in Khulna
item.description:
The month-long tree fair at Khulna Circuit House Ground is drawing large crowds as visitors flock to explore a wide range of local and exotic plant varieties.
Organised jointly by the Khulna district administration and the Sundarban West Forest Department, the fair began on July 11 to promote tree plantation and raise environmental awareness, particularly among younger people.
According to the fair's control room, 62 organisations, including 10 government agencies, are participating in this year's event. The fair remains open daily from 9am with free entry.
As of Monday, around 37,570 saplings worth Tk 54,27,620 had been sold, reflecting strong public interest.
Rare and exotic saplings have emerged as major attractions, including the medicinal Corossol Tree, believed to have cancer-preventive properties, the Ghugu Pakhi variety and Star Jui, which is priced at Tk15,000 per plant.
Fruit trees, particularly mango saplings, are among the best-selling items, while urban gardeners are showing growing interest in dwarf and early-fruiting varieties suitable for rooftops and small spaces. Flowering plants, orchids and tub-friendly fruit plants are also in high demand.
"The price of fruit plants that bear year-round ranges from Tk800 to Tk1,500," said Abu Masud, owner of Dalia Nursery. He said his stall features a range of fruit plants aimed at urban gardeners, alongside moringa saplings grown from seeds sourced from India.
Visitors said they came to expand their rooftop gardens with fruit and ornamental plants.
"I bought a moringa plant, a Japanese cherry blossom plant and several varieties of roses," said Sithi Islam, a resident of Nirala.
Farzana Mithila of Hazi Mohsin Road said she purchased fruit and flower plants, along with three lojjaboti saplings.
Md Zakir Hossain, duty officer at the fair's control room, said adequate security measures had been put in place for traders and visitors.
The annual fair has been a popular event in Khulna for nearly a decade, attracting nature lovers and gardening enthusiasts from across the city.

item.title: Bumper harvest, fair prices lift Rajshahi jute growers
item.description:
After years of low returns and rising production costs, jute farmers in Rajshahi are finally seeing a turnaround as strong prices and a bumper harvest breathe new life into the country's traditional ‘golden fibre.’
Freshly harvested jute is selling for Tk4,000-4,500 per maund, up sharply from Tk3,000-3,500 at the start of last season, allowing growers to recover costs comfortably and earn healthy profits.
The improved market has also fuelled optimism that jute could reclaim its position as one of the country's most profitable cash crops if prices remain stable throughout the harvesting season.
At Nowhata Haat in Paba upazila on Monday, trading was brisk as farmers arrived with freshly processed fibre loaded onto vans, three-wheelers and locally made Nosimon vehicles.
Bablu Ahmed of Choubaria village, who cultivated an early jute variety on five bighas, said he harvested around 11 maunds per bigha and sold part of his produce at Tk4,500 per maund.
"After covering production costs, I'm expecting a profit of around Tk25,000 per bigha," he said.
Abdul Alim of Bargachhi Union said he spent nearly Tk22,000 to cultivate each bigha of land this season. With favourable weather producing yields of 10-12 maunds per bigha, he expects to earn around Tk20,000 in profit per bigha.
Traders also reported a much stronger market than last year.
"Last season we bought jute for Tk3,000 to Tk3,500 per maund. This year we're paying around Tk4,500, and even more for premium-quality fibre," said trader Janip Hossain of Nowhata Bazar.
Across Paba, farmers are simultaneously harvesting jute and preparing fields for Aman paddy transplantation. While encouraged by the current prices, many remain wary that rates could fall once peak-season supplies enter the market.
They also cited labour shortages and inadequate water bodies for retting, forcing them to transport harvested jute over long distances and increasing production costs.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), jute cultivation in Rajshahi has expanded to 18,399 hectares this season, up from 17,305 hectares last year. The district has set a production target of 49,333 metric tonnes, compared with 48,677 metric tonnes produced last year.
Rajshahi DAE Deputy Director Mohammad Nasir Uddin said the crop initially faced setbacks due to drought and a diesel shortage. However, timely rainfall, improved fuel supplies and proper crop management helped farmers achieve good yields.
"The current market price is encouraging. Farmers are expected to make better profits this year, which will have a positive impact on the rural economy," he said.
Paba Upazila Agriculture Officer MA Mannan said sustained prices throughout the season could encourage more farmers to expand jute cultivation next year.
Meanwhile, Assistant Director of the Department of Jute in Rajshahi Md Nadim Akhtar said production is projected to reach 381,696 quintals this year, up from 360,494 quintals last year.
He said the combination of higher output and favourable prices has created fresh optimism among growers, who believe a stable market could help restore jute's importance in Bangladesh's agricultural economy.

item.title: DU to review 15 years of appointments, investigate teachers over July uprising
item.description:
Dhaka University's (DU) Syndicate has decided to review all appointments of teachers, officers and staff made between January 1, 2009, and June 30, 2024, while also launching an investigation into allegations against teachers accused of opposing students during the July 2024 mass uprising.
The decisions were taken at a Syndicate meeting on Tuesday, chaired by Vice-Chancellor Prof ABM Obaidul Islam, who confirmed them to Dhaka Tribune.
To review appointments made during the period, the Syndicate formed an investigation committee headed by Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Academic) Prof Abdus Salam. Deans of the university's various faculties will serve as members of the committee.
The Syndicate also decided to review research activities carried out under the World Bank- and University Grants Commission (UGC)-funded Higher Education Quality Enhancement Project (HEQEP) during the same period to determine whether project funds were properly utilised.
A separate committee, headed by Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Administration) Prof Mohammed Almujaddade Alfasane, has been formed to conduct the review.
The Syndicate also constituted a four-member committee to investigate allegations against teachers accused of taking a stand against students during the July 2024 mass uprising.
The committee comprises the vice-chancellor, the two pro-vice-chancellors and Syndicate member Prof Morshed Hasan Khan. It will examine a list of 125 teachers submitted by the platform Dhaka Bisshobiddyaloyer Fyasibad-birodhi Shikkhok-mondoli to determine whether they opposed students during the uprising.
According to the decisions taken at the meeting, if any accused teacher is found to be affiliated with a teachers' organization, action may also be taken against that organization.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune, Alfasane said a list had been submitted naming teachers accused of being aligned with forces that opposed the 2024 mass uprising.
He said that if the committee's investigation finds any teacher responsible, disciplinary action will be taken. If any organization is found to have been involved, action will also be taken against it.
"The committee will thoroughly examine the video footage, photographs and news reports submitted as evidence before identifying those responsible and recommending appropriate measures. If any organization is found to be involved, we will take action against it as well," he said.
Meanwhile, activists from Ducsu, hall unions and Islami Chhatra Shibir demonstrated outside the Syndicate meeting, alleging that it was preparing to approve a revised hall seat-allocation policy that would allow irregular students to stay in university residence halls for an additional year.
The protesters used a handheld microphone outside the venue, with the sound reportedly carrying into the meeting hall.
Amid the protests, the proposed policy was not approved.
The vice-chancellor said a final decision would be taken after further discussions with the relevant stakeholders.
He also said the university would review footage of those who used the handheld microphone outside the venue to project sound into the meeting hall.
The Syndicate also imposed disciplinary measures of varying severity and duration against several teachers over separate allegations. Explaining the decision to relieve Mehidy Hasan Miraz of the captaincy, Tamim praised his leadership but said the all-rounder was needed more as a performer.

He also indicated that Miraz could return to a leadership role in the future, citing his significant contribution to Bangladesh cricket.
Tamim said injury management was a major factor behind opting against three different captains across the formats.
He revealed that the growing number of injuries among the country's fast bowlers had made workload management increasingly important.
"When there are three captains, each wants to field the best bowlers in his format, which puts extra pressure on the players. With separate white-ball and red-ball captains, they can coordinate better and manage workloads more effectively," he said.

item.title: Alleged top criminal David Emon arrested in Jessore
item.description:
Detective Branch (DB) police on Wednesday arrested alleged top criminal Mobarak Hossain Emon, also known as David Emon, in Jessore.
Jessore Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime) Mirajul Islam confirmed the arrest to Dhaka Tribune at around 2pm.
"DB police arrested David Emon from a vehicle in the Jhumjhumpur area on the Jessore-Narail Highway. He is now in the custody of Jessore police. Details will be provided later," he said.
According to police, Emon and Mohammad Raihan allegedly took over leadership of a criminal syndicate in Chittagong after the arrest of Chhoto Sajjad, an alleged associate of fugitive criminal Sajjad Ali Khan. Investigators alleged that Chhoto Sajjad had previously carried out criminal activities on behalf of Boro Sajjad.
Police said followers of Sajjad Ali Khan have been behind most recent extortion demands and attacks in Chittagong city and the upazilas of Raozan, Hathazari and Fatikchhari. Law enforcement agencies had been searching for both Emon and Raihan before Wednesday's arrest.
One of the cases linked to Emon is an alleged extortion attempt targeting Digital Dot Net (DDN), a Chittagong-based business.
According to police, DDN owner Adil Bin Mamun received a call from a foreign number on July 11 from a person identifying himself as David Emon, who allegedly demanded Tk20 million in extortion and threatened further attacks if the money was not paid.
Police said that two days later, at around 12:30pm on July 13, about 30 to 35 armed men attacked the DDN office on the Chandanpura-Bakalia Access Road under Chawkbazar Police Station.
The assailants allegedly vandalized the office, looted Tk3.5 million kept there for salary payments and warned the company against continuing its operations. CCTV footage of the attack later circulated on social media.
Police said the attacked office is adjacent to the residence of Smart Group Director Mujibur Rahman, where gunfire was reported on February 28 while the house was under police protection. Investigators alleged that followers of fugitive criminal Sajjad Ali Khan carried out the attack after failing to extort money from the businessman.
The same residence also came under gunfire on January 2, when bullets struck its windows and doors. Police protection remained in place following the incident.
Earlier, Chittagong police arrested two alleged associates of Emon from the Wazedia area on the Oxygen-Kuaish Road, recovering a foreign-made pistol and four rounds of ammunition.
The suspects, identified as Md Asif, 25, and Saidul Islam, alias Arif, 24, were arrested on Sunday night. Police said Asif was a fugitive accused in a criminal case.
